### 4.4 WebSocket events

Envelope:

```json
{
  "server_id": "uuid",
  "epoch": "uuid",
  "revision": 1042,
  "type": "changed",
  "resource": {"kind": "session", "id": "record-uuid"},
  "at_ms": 1760220000000
}
```

Event types:

- `hello {epoch, revision}`: the first frame on every subscription.
- **Scope.** A listing leaves out the records Dispatch made for its own use: a ticket's project with everything in it, and a worker session (the planner, an implementer, a reviewer) in any project, told by the `<ticket>-<nonce>` form of the op they were made under (`switchboard_control::is_dispatch_worker_op`). A supervisor's records (`sup-…`) and the owner's own are listed as ever, and a worker record is still read by its id, which is how the ticket view to come will reach them. `?scope=all` on `projects`, `sessions`, `waiting` and on the `events` subscription lists them and announces them; a plain subscription gets no `project`, `sessions`, `session` or `runs` frame about one. `info` lists
- `changed {kind, id}` with the **metadata kinds** `project`, `space`, `set`, `session`; the **content kinds** `conversation`, `screen`, `run_output` (`id` = `record/n`), `file` (a pinned file, `id` = `project_id/path`); and the collection kinds `projects`, `spaces`, `sets` (with the space's id), `sessions` (with the project's id), `runs` (with the record's id), `waiting`, emitted when a collection's member id set moves and answered by refetching the collection whole; a global collection's `id` is the empty string. Each kind is its own resource key on the client (§4.2); a member fetched as part of its collection holds the collection's revision until it is read alone.
- `removed {kind, id}`: the resource is gone; the client drops it and marks any window on it "removed on <server>".
- `watching {kind, id}`: the answer to a `watch` frame (below).
- `resync_required`: sent before the host closes a subscriber whose queue overflowed; the client reconnects and refetches everything.

**What produces events.** The host has no event bus, and a save is not a reliable sign of a visible change: working sets save through `SaveViews`, Claude Code's trust question (`PromptSeen`) and a Codex pane going quiet (`HostListed`) change what a card says with no save at all. So the port does not watch for saves. Revision and events come from three places in `app.rs`:

1. **The read-model diff, after every pass.** After every `dispatch` and after every polling pass (`HostListed`, the hook log, `Tick`), the app recomputes a cheap per-resource fingerprint of each exported metadata read model (`SessionView`, `SetView` with its members, `ProjectView`, `SpaceView`, `waiting`) and compares it with the previous pass's. One `changed` per resource whose fingerprint moved, one `removed` per resource that vanished, one `changed` per collection whose membership moved, and `revision` bumped once per pass that emitted anything. The diff is the gate, not the effect list, so a set rename, a pin edit, a trust-question transition, a quiet-state transition and a time-based r
2. **Content versions, assigned where content is read.** Conversation text, pane text, run output and pinned files are mutable outside the core and can change between two reads inside one poll interval, so a content reply's revision cannot come from the counter alone. Every content read goes through a per-key **content cache** in `SwitchboardApp`, whose bookkeeping lives on the frame and whose reads run on the connection or worker thread (§4.1). The cache holds, per key, the **source version** and the **policy fingerprint of the owning project (§4.3)** it last served, with the revision it was assigned. The source version per kind, chosen so that no change the host can see leaves it unchanged
   - **transcript**: size and mtime. Claude Code's JSONL only appends, Switchboard never edits one, and `/clear` or a discard rebinds the record to another file, so a growing size is a reliable version and a same-size rewrite does not occur;
   - **pinned file**: inode, ctime and size, read from the descriptor the walk ends on. No user tool preserves ctime, so an editor that rewrites in place, a same-size rewrite, and a replace-by-rename (a new inode) all move it;
   - **run output**: inode, ctime and size of the run's log. A log truncated and regrown to the same length has a new ctime; a rotated one a new inode;
   - **screen**: a hash of the pane text, as today.
   When either the source version or the policy fingerprint differs from what the cache holds, the worker's reply carries the new content and the frame, on the worker's version action, bumps `revision`, emits `changed {content kind, id}`, and stores the new version with that revision; the reply is stamped with that revision. **Two different content versions never share a revision for one key within an epoch**, and two reads of unchanged content return the same bytes and the same revision. The policy is resolved before the read; a resolution failure refuses the reply and leaves the cache untouched, so no earlier masked bytes stand in for the answer. A policy change is also noticed by the diff
3. **The watch poll.** The port keeps a **watch set**: every content key any subscriber has asked to watch, plus every content key read in the last minute. Independently of the local view, every two seconds a worker thread checks each watched key's source version (a `stat`, or a pane snapshot for `screen`; never a parse) and, for a key that moved, reads it through the content cache, which is what emits the `changed`. The local session view reads its conversation through the same cache (an unmasked variant; §4.3), so the two polls share work rather than duplicate it. The set is capped at 128 keys (§4.1); past that the least recently read key is dropped, and a key with no subscriber and no rea

**Watch frames.** A client sends `watch {kind, id}` when the first view instance on a content key opens and `unwatch` when the last one closes; the client keeps a reference count per key so closing one of two windows on a session changes nothing on the host. The host answers `watching` once the key is in its set, and the client fetches the initial content only after that, so the first snapshot's revision is covered by the poll from then on. A watch is never refused. On reconnect, after `hello`, the client resends every watch with a nonzero count before it snapshots. A visible content view also refetches on its own every thirty seconds, which is what covers a key the host evicted from the set

**The conversation cache** moves from `UiState` to `SwitchboardApp` as one of the content caches, keyed by record id, resume handle and content version, read by the session view and the port alike; `UiState` keeps a reference, not a copy. This is a frontend change (the session, card and workflow views read the cache), so it is its own commit before any port code, Milestone A0 (§10), with the app behaving identically. This, the diff and the worker handoff are the changes to the app outside the adapter, and §12.6 says why they are required.

**Subscribe first, then snapshot.** A client connecting to a host:

1. opens the WebSocket and waits for `hello {epoch, revision}` (events start flowing at once and are buffered by the client);
2. fetches the snapshots it needs, each reply carrying its own `revision`;
3. applies the buffered events: an event whose `revision` is past a snapshot's `revision` invalidates that resource and is refetched; the rest were already in the snapshot;
4. enables commands.

Because the subscriber is registered on the frame thread before any later pass can bump `revision`, a metadata snapshot is taken on that thread with the revision it carries, and a content reply is stamped on that thread when the worker's version action lands (the same moment its `changed` would be emitted, so the event and the reply name one revision), no change can fall between a subscription and a snapshot. Several snapshots in flight are each reconciled against the buffer by their own revision; events that arrive during a refetch are reconciled the same way, which is why the client never clears its buffer until step 4. A resource named by an event the client has never seen is fetched. If 

### 4.3 Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Wire body | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/info` | new: `info` | none (identity only, before pairing) |
| POST | `/api/v1/pair` | pairing handshake (§5) | none, only inside the pairing window |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects` | `projects`; `?scope=all` includes Dispatch's worker records | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/spaces` | `spaces` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/spaces/{id}/sets` | `sets` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sets/{id}` | new: `set` (the `SetView` with pins) | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{id}/sessions` | `sessions`; `?scope=all` as above | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}` | `session` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/waiting` | `waiting`; `?scope=all` as above | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/screen?lines=n` | `session.screen` | read |
207:- `session.last_response`: the last turn's `final_text`, its `n` and `end`. It is a **projection of the `conversation` key**: it is read from the same cache, carries the conversation's content revision, is watched by watching `conversation`, and refreshes on `changed {conversation}`; a window showing only the last response registers that watch. The compact card's one-line excerpt is not part of it: that is `last_message` from the `Stop` hook on the record, a field of the session's metadata, and moves with `changed {session}`.
    }
}

/// What an agent card says under its title: the first line of the last
/// answer, else what the agent is doing, else the prompt it is on.
fn agent_excerpt(c: &Conversation) -> Option<String> {
    let turn = c.turns.last()?;
    let first_line = |text: &str| {
        text.lines()
            .map(|l| l.trim().trim_start_matches(['#', '-', '*', '>']).trim())
            .find(|l| !l.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_owned)
    };

## The decisions the issue asks for

**1. Trust in the certificate: the click-through is the trust step.**
Why not the download: Apple's evaluation refuses today's certificate
even as the only trusted anchor, "certificate name does not match
input", because it has no subjectAltName (Facts, Settled, spike 23
`README.md:46`; `make_identity` builds `CertificateParams::new(vec![])`,
`src/adapters/remote.rs:103`). A trusted install therefore needs a
reissue with an IP SAN, bound to one address, so every DHCP change
means a new certificate and a new trust step on every phone (Settled,
`README.md:47`, `:50`). That is a larger feature than this page, and
the click-through needs none of it. What the click buys: the browser
accepts this certificate for this address. What it does not: it proves
nothing about who answered; on a hostile LAN an impostor can serve a
genuine-looking page and ask for the code. The code is single-use, the
window five minutes and three tries, and the owner compares the Key
line the page shows with the dialog's. The dialog says that in one
sentence. §5 is kept: before pairing the port serves `/info`, `/pair`
and the three page paths, nothing else.
Rests on two Unresolved lines: whether Safari offers a click-through for
a CN-only certificate on an IP, and whether the `wss://` socket then
connects (WebKit 41419 suggests it may not). The page is built for the
second regardless (polling fallback, UI). **Fallback if the owner's
device says there is no click-through:** `make_identity` takes the
advertised addresses and writes an IP SAN for each, the serverAuth EKU,
`not_before` kept at 1975 (the 825-day rule binds certificates issued
after 2019-07-01, Settled), the same key so the SPKI pin holds;
`identity.json` keeps the certificate, reissued when
`remote::local_address()` changes; a fourth page path `/switchboard.cer`
serves it; the dialog tells the owner to trust it under Certificate
Trust Settings (Settled, support.apple.com/en-us/102390).

**2. The credential is a cookie.** `/pair`, when the body carries
`"credential": "cookie"`, sets
`__Host-sb-<server_id>=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`
(400 days, the cap, Settled) and leaves `token` out of the JSON.
Native clients do not send the field and get the token as before. The
name carries the server id because cookies are not isolated by port and
`__Host-` does not change that (Settled, RFC 6265 §8.5), so two hosts on
one IP do not overwrite each other. `SameSite=Strict` does not stop a
request from another port on the same IP (Settled, "site" ignores the
port), so the host checks `Origin` itself: a cookie-authenticated
request is refused 403 `origin` unless `Origin` equals
`https://<Host header>`, and a cookie-authenticated non-GET request or
upgrade without an `Origin` is refused too (a browser always sends one
for those; a plain GET may omit it and is side-effect free). A request
carrying a bearer header skips the check. The WebSocket handshake
carries the cookie and an `Origin` (Settled, WHATWG §2.2; RFC 6455
§10.2) and needs no subprotocol, so `respond_upgrade` is unchanged.
Rests on the Unresolved line "whether a `Secure` cookie on a
click-through origin is stored and sent". **Fallback if the owner's
device shows it is not:** the `/pair` reply keeps `token` for the page,
the page sends `Authorization: Bearer` on `fetch` and offers
`["sb1", <token>]` to `new WebSocket`; `read_request` keeps
`sec-websocket-protocol`, and `respond_upgrade` echoes `sb1` (a base64url
token fits RFC 6455's token rule, Settled); the token lives in
`localStorage`, which Safari deletes after seven days without use
(Settled), so the marker then reads "not paired" and the owner pairs
again.

**3. One QR, two texts.** The QR becomes the URL
`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (a
smaller QR than the JSON: version 8 against 9, Settled, `README.md:61`).
"Copy invite" stays the JSON, so `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`,
the headset's paste field and the per-line scan
(`client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:111`,
`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`) and the
assertion at `tests/ui.rs:7474`–`7492` keep working, and the Swift tests
(not in CI) are not touched. A "Copy link" button copies the URL. This
is the "Keep JSON" branch of For the owner; if the owner wants URL only,
the implementer teaches `PairingInvite.parse`
(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`, `parse`) the URL with
`URLComponents` (an IPv6 literal arrives in brackets and is an
Unresolved parsing question), changes the assertion at
`tests/ui.rs:7486`, and adds a Swift fixture test.

**4. The static paths.** Exactly `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
`GET /app.css` (`text/css; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js`
(`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`); the query is ignored, so
`/?code=…` is `/`. Any other method or path falls through to the frame
and is refused 404 as today (`/favicon.ico`, `/index.html`, `HEAD /`).
The page's icon is `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no browser asks
for `/favicon.ico` unprompted. Headers on the three:
`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`
(`'self'` covers `wss://` on the same host and port, Settled; the policy
is a header because `frame-ancestors` is ignored in a `<meta>`, Settled),
`Cache-Control: no-store` (the files change with the binary and are
small), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
`Connection: close`. These are answered **on the connection thread**,
before `RemoteIncoming` is built, so a page load costs no frame pass, no
inbox slot (`FRAMES`/64) and none of the eight drains per pass
(`DRAIN_PER_PASS`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:580`), and it works with the
app hidden. `Connection: close` ends the thread and so frees the
connection's slot in the four-connection unauthenticated pool at once.
Their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120`, beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE`
and `INFO_PER_MINUTE` (`:583`–`:584`), through `Limits::limited`
(`:631`), 429 as the others. A page opened with no code and no cookie
shows "This browser is not paired" and how to pair (Remote devices…,
Allow pairing, scan the QR); a code whose window has closed shows the
host's `pairing_closed` text.
Rests on the Unresolved line about Safari's parallel connections against
`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`. The page loads its two files after the HTML
and calls `/info` and then `/pair` one at a time, so at most three
connections are open at once, and it retries a network error three times
300 ms apart. **Fallback if the owner's device still sees a refused
connection:** raise `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` to 6 and amend §4.1's first
bound; the pools stay separate.

**5. Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/index.html`,
`web/app.css`, `web/app.js` at the repo root, embedded by
`src/adapters/web.rs` with `include_str!`. No build step, no
dependency, no `build.rs`. `Cargo.toml` excludes only
`vendor/egui_term` (`:91`), so `web/` ships in the crate. Tests below.

**6. The device record.** No change (Record, below).

## The page

`app.js`, plain ES2020, no `eval`, `innerHTML` or `document.write`
(text through `textContent`, which is the whole XSS argument for a page
that can type into an agent). In order:

1. First statement: read `location.search`, then
   `history.replaceState(null, "", location.pathname)`; the code lives
   in a variable only, never in storage. (Whether the browser's global
   history or iCloud tab sync kept the first URL is Unresolved; the
   dialog's text does not promise it did not.)
2. `GET /api/v1/info`. With an invite: if `spki_sha256` or `server_id`
   differs from `key`/`id`, say "this is not the host the code was made
   for" and send nothing. Else show the host name, the short key (four
   groups of four, as the dialog does), the name field and a Pair
   button; the tap posts `/pair {spki_sha256: key, code, device_name,
   credential: "cookie"}`. `wrong_code`, `wrong_key`, `pairing_closed`
   and `rate_limited` are worded plainly.
3. Without an invite: `GET /me`; 200 shows the list, 401 per the
   marker (departures, above).
4. The list follows §4.4: open the socket, wait for `hello`, fetch
   `projects`, `waiting` and each project's `sessions` (the listing
   has no global form), apply buffered events by revision (an event
   past a snapshot's revision refetches that resource). A "Waiting on
   you" band comes first, then projects, waiting sessions first in each
   and marked; each row shows kind (`claude`, `codex`, `shell`,
   `command`, `service`), the card word, `waiting_reason` and the
   excerpt of departure 1. The header shows the host name from `/info`,
   and this device's name and scope from `/me`.
5. A session view: `claude`/`codex` read `last-response`, falling back
   to `screen` when it is empty; the rest read `screen`; a session not
   running shows its liveness and exit code (run output is a later
   issue, per "Not in this cut"). It watches the key and refetches on
   `changed`, and on its own every thirty seconds (§4.4).
6. The reply box exists only when `/me` says `control`. A send posts
   `{op: <uuid>, text}` to `/sessions/{id}/send`; the op is kept in
   `sessionStorage` until the reply is read, a timeout is followed by
   `GET /ops/{op}`, never a resend (§4.5), and a reload with a pending
   op asks `/ops/{op}` first. A 403 `scope` hides the box again. The
   op id is `crypto.randomUUID()` where present, else 16 bytes from
   `crypto.getRandomValues` (the Unresolved line on certificate-error
   pages).
7. Live updates: if `hello` does not arrive within five seconds, or the
   socket closes before `hello` twice running, the page says "live
   updates unavailable, refreshing every 5 s" and polls `waiting` and the
   open session every five seconds, projects and sessions every
   fifteen. This is the answer to the `wss://` Unresolved line and
   stays in whichever way the owner's run goes.

  does not stop an active relay that terminates TLS and forwards both
  `/info` and `/pair`. The dialog says so (UI, below).

  `/pair` reply to a browser omits `token` (below).
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused"** stops being true for
  three exact paths. `docs/remote-client.md:306` ("Require pairing

  the plan keeps the JSON (the issue allows it). The Swift side is not

  met by the page's `/me` on load and by a socket close followed by a

## The decisions the issue asks for

**1. Trust in the certificate: the click-through is the trust step.**
Why not the download: Apple's evaluation refuses today's certificate
even as the only trusted anchor, "certificate name does not match
input", because it has no subjectAltName (Facts, Settled, spike 23
`README.md:46`; `make_identity` builds `CertificateParams::new(vec![])`,
`src/adapters/remote.rs:103`). A trusted install therefore needs a
reissue with an IP SAN, bound to one address, so every DHCP change
means a new certificate and a new trust step on every phone (Settled,
`README.md:47`, `:50`). That is a larger feature than this page, and
the click-through needs none of it. What the click buys: the browser
accepts this certificate for this address. What it does not: it proves
nothing about who answered; on a hostile LAN an impostor can serve a
genuine-looking page and ask for the code. The code is single-use, the
window five minutes and three tries, and the owner compares the Key
line the page shows with the dialog's. The dialog says that in one
sentence. §5 is kept: before pairing the port serves `/info`, `/pair`
and the three page paths, nothing else.
Rests on two Unresolved lines: whether Safari offers a click-through for
a CN-only certificate on an IP, and whether the `wss://` socket then
connects (WebKit 41419 suggests it may not). The page is built for the
second regardless (polling fallback, UI). **Fallback if the owner's
device says there is no click-through:** `make_identity` takes the
advertised addresses and writes an IP SAN for each, the serverAuth EKU,
`not_before` kept at 1975 (the 825-day rule binds certificates issued
after 2019-07-01, Settled), the same key so the SPKI pin holds;
`identity.json` keeps the certificate, reissued when
`remote::local_address()` changes; a fourth page path `/switchboard.cer`
serves it; the dialog tells the owner to trust it under Certificate
Trust Settings (Settled, support.apple.com/en-us/102390).

**2. The credential is a cookie.** `/pair`, when the body carries
`"credential": "cookie"`, sets
`__Host-sb-<server_id>=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`
(400 days, the cap, Settled) and leaves `token` out of the JSON.
Native clients do not send the field and get the token as before. The
name carries the server id because cookies are not isolated by port and
`__Host-` does not change that (Settled, RFC 6265 §8.5), so two hosts on
one IP do not overwrite each other. `SameSite=Strict` does not stop a
request from another port on the same IP (Settled, "site" ignores the
port), so the host checks `Origin` itself: a cookie-authenticated
request is refused 403 `origin` unless `Origin` equals
`https://<Host header>`, and a cookie-authenticated non-GET request or
upgrade without an `Origin` is refused too (a browser always sends one
for those; a plain GET may omit it and is side-effect free). A request
carrying a bearer header skips the check. The WebSocket handshake
carries the cookie and an `Origin` (Settled, WHATWG §2.2; RFC 6455
§10.2) and needs no subprotocol, so `respond_upgrade` is unchanged.
Rests on the Unresolved line "whether a `Secure` cookie on a
click-through origin is stored and sent". **Fallback if the owner's
device shows it is not:** the `/pair` reply keeps `token` for the page,
the page sends `Authorization: Bearer` on `fetch` and offers
`["sb1", <token>]` to `new WebSocket`; `read_request` keeps
`sec-websocket-protocol`, and `respond_upgrade` echoes `sb1` (a base64url
token fits RFC 6455's token rule, Settled); the token lives in
`localStorage`, which Safari deletes after seven days without use
(Settled), so the marker then reads "not paired" and the owner pairs
again.

**3. One QR, two texts.** The QR becomes the URL
`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (a
smaller QR than the JSON: version 8 against 9, Settled, `README.md:61`).
"Copy invite" stays the JSON, so `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`,
the headset's paste field and the per-line scan
(`client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:111`,
`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`) and the
assertion at `tests/ui.rs:7474`–`7492` keep working, and the Swift tests
(not in CI) are not touched. A "Copy link" button copies the URL. This
is the "Keep JSON" branch of For the owner; if the owner wants URL only,
the implementer teaches `PairingInvite.parse`
(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`, `parse`) the URL with
`URLComponents` (an IPv6 literal arrives in brackets and is an
Unresolved parsing question), changes the assertion at
`tests/ui.rs:7486`, and adds a Swift fixture test.

**4. The static paths.** Exactly `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
`GET /app.css` (`text/css; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js`
(`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`); the query is ignored, so
`/?code=…` is `/`. Any other method or path falls through to the frame
and is refused 404 as today (`/favicon.ico`, `/index.html`, `HEAD /`).
The page's icon is `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no browser asks
for `/favicon.ico` unprompted. Headers on the three:
`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`
(`'self'` covers `wss://` on the same host and port, Settled; the policy
is a header because `frame-ancestors` is ignored in a `<meta>`, Settled),
`Cache-Control: no-store` (the files change with the binary and are
small), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
`Connection: close`. These are answered **on the connection thread**,
before `RemoteIncoming` is built, so a page load costs no frame pass, no
inbox slot (`FRAMES`/64) and none of the eight drains per pass
(`DRAIN_PER_PASS`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:580`), and it works with the
app hidden. `Connection: close` ends the thread and so frees the
connection's slot in the four-connection unauthenticated pool at once.
Their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120`, beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE`
and `INFO_PER_MINUTE` (`:583`–`:584`), through `Limits::limited`
(`:631`), 429 as the others. A page opened with no code and no cookie
shows "This browser is not paired" and how to pair (Remote devices…,
Allow pairing, scan the QR); a code whose window has closed shows the
host's `pairing_closed` text.
Rests on the Unresolved line about Safari's parallel connections against
`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`. The page loads its two files after the HTML
and calls `/info` and then `/pair` one at a time, so at most three
connections are open at once, and it retries a network error three times
300 ms apart. **Fallback if the owner's device still sees a refused
connection:** raise `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` to 6 and amend §4.1's first
bound; the pools stay separate.

**5. Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/index.html`,
`web/app.css`, `web/app.js` at the repo root, embedded by
`src/adapters/web.rs` with `include_str!`. No build step, no
dependency, no `build.rs`. `Cargo.toml` excludes only
`vendor/egui_term` (`:91`), so `web/` ships in the crate. Tests below.

**6. The device record.** No change (Record, below).

## The record

Nothing changes on disk. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`)
like any other: `name` is the `device_name` `/pair` already takes
(`src/app.rs:3650`, cut to 64 characters by `new_device`), `scope` comes
from the pairing window, it is listed and revoked in the dialog as today.
The page offers a name field defaulted from the user agent ("Safari on
iPhone", "Chrome on Android"; an iPad reads as "Safari on Mac", Settled),
which the owner can edit before pairing, so the host parses no user
agent. Nothing marks a device as a browser. Rehydration is today's: the
hash of the cookie's token goes through `device_by_token`, so a browser
paired yesterday is authenticated today.
Schema versions today: `SCHEMA_VERSION` 16 (`src/core/model.rs:12`),
`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION` 7 (`:612`), `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1
(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). No serialized type changes, so none bumps;
if a ticket landing in parallel changes one, that ticket's bump is its
own (from the value at implementation time, plus one).

## The signals

- `RemoteRequest` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:360`) gains `cookie`,
  `origin` and `host`, taken in `read_request` (`:444`) beside
  `authorization`, which today is the only credential kept. Like the
  bearer they are never logged; `refuse` (`src/app.rs:3754`) logs method
  and path only and no log line prints a query or token (Facts, Settled).
  `RemoteRequest::cookie_origin_ok()` is the Origin rule of decision 2.
- `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains `set_cookie: Option<String>`; every
  literal in `src/app.rs` (about fourteen, e.g. `:1664`, `:1679`,
  `:2365`, `:2754`, `:3570`, `:3723`, `:3736`, `:3767`) and
  `adapters/remote.rs:829` gets `set_cookie: None`.
- `respond` (`:530`), which hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json`,
  becomes a wrapper over `respond_with(w, status, content_type, extra
  headers, body)`; the page and the `Set-Cookie` use the second.
- `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`): bearer first; else the cookie
  named for this host's server id, then the Origin rule. A refusal is
  403 `origin` ("this request did not come from the page the host
  served") or the same 401s as today.
- The events socket: nothing new. `changed` with `session`, `sessions`,
  `projects`, `waiting`, `conversation` and `screen` kinds (the
  spec's §4.4) is all the page reads; it sends
  `{"type":"watch","resource":{"kind":"screen"|"conversation","id":…}}`
  for the open session (`src/app.rs:1720`).

## The actions and effects

None. No `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no port method: everything is
adapter, `serve_remote` and the page. In `serve_remote` (`:3017`) `/pair`
reads the `credential` field and builds the `Set-Cookie`; a new
authenticated arm `("GET", ["me"])` answers `{device_id, name, scope}`
in the usual envelope. `core/remote.rs` gains one pure function,
`pairing_url(addr: SocketAddr, server_id, spki_sha256, code) -> String`
(`SocketAddr`'s display brackets an IPv6 literal; the code's alphabet
and hex need no percent-encoding).

## The page

`app.js`, plain ES2020, no `eval`, `innerHTML` or `document.write`
(text through `textContent`, which is the whole XSS argument for a page
that can type into an agent). In order:

1. First statement: read `location.search`, then
   `history.replaceState(null, "", location.pathname)`; the code lives
   in a variable only, never in storage. (Whether the browser's global
   history or iCloud tab sync kept the first URL is Unresolved; the
   dialog's text does not promise it did not.)
2. `GET /api/v1/info`. With an invite: if `spki_sha256` or `server_id`
   differs from `key`/`id`, say "this is not the host the code was made
   for" and send nothing. Else show the host name, the short key (four
   groups of four, as the dialog does), the name field and a Pair
   button; the tap posts `/pair {spki_sha256: key, code, device_name,
   credential: "cookie"}`. `wrong_code`, `wrong_key`, `pairing_closed`
   and `rate_limited` are worded plainly.
3. Without an invite: `GET /me`; 200 shows the list, 401 per the
   marker (departures, above).
4. The list follows §4.4: open the socket, wait for `hello`, fetch
   `projects`, `waiting` and each project's `sessions` (the listing
   has no global form), apply buffered events by revision (an event
   past a snapshot's revision refetches that resource). A "Waiting on
   you" band comes first, then projects, waiting sessions first in each
   and marked; each row shows kind (`claude`, `codex`, `shell`,
   `command`, `service`), the card word, `waiting_reason` and the
   excerpt of departure 1. The header shows the host name from `/info`,
   and this device's name and scope from `/me`.
5. A session view: `claude`/`codex` read `last-response`, falling back
   to `screen` when it is empty; the rest read `screen`; a session not
   running shows its liveness and exit code (run output is a later
   issue, per "Not in this cut"). It watches the key and refetches on
   `changed`, and on its own every thirty seconds (§4.4).
6. The reply box exists only when `/me` says `control`. A send posts
   `{op: <uuid>, text}` to `/sessions/{id}/send`; the op is kept in
   `sessionStorage` until the reply is read, a timeout is followed by
   `GET /ops/{op}`, never a resend (§4.5), and a reload with a pending
   op asks `/ops/{op}` first. A 403 `scope` hides the box again. The
   op id is `crypto.randomUUID()` where present, else 16 bytes from
   `crypto.getRandomValues` (the Unresolved line on certificate-error
   pages).
7. Live updates: if `hello` does not arrive within five seconds, or the
   socket closes before `hello` twice running, the page says "live
   updates unavailable, refreshing every 5 s" and polls `waiting` and the
   open session every five seconds, projects and sessions every
   fifteen. This is the answer to the `wss://` Unresolved line and
   stays in whichever way the owner's run goes.

## The UI

`src/ui/remote.rs`: the QR (`qr_texture`, `:280`) encodes
`pairing_url(...)`; `payload` stays the JSON for "Copy invite"; a "Copy
link" button beside it. Address, port and the cache key (`draft.qr`
keyed by code, `:168`) as today. The scan line becomes: "Scan with a
phone camera to open the page, or paste the invite into a client.
The browser will warn about the certificate; accepting it is the trust
step, so check that the page shows this Key. Grants {scope} scope. Open

ends "only paired devices get past /info and the page". With the port on

behaviour, now inherited); listed as a known gap, not fixed here.

1	# Plan for issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port
2	
3	One commit. The app runs at every step: the page is served beside the
4	API and nothing the native clients speak changes. Line numbers are this
5	worktree's (HEAD 380e4d4). "Facts" is `facts/1/repo/facts.md`; a line
6	cited as Settled is not re-derived here, and every decision that rests
7	on an Unresolved or For-the-owner line says so where it is made and
8	names the fallback.
9	
10	## Where this departs from the issue
11	
12	- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.** The Mac
13	  computes it in the UI (`agent_excerpt`, `src/ui/cards.rs:558`);
14	  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no excerpt, and
15	  `docs/remote-client.md:207` describes a `last_message` field on the
16	  session's metadata that the code does not have (Facts, Settled:
17	  `waiting` and the listings carry no excerpt). The page shows what the
18	  view has: the card word, `waiting_reason`, kind, liveness, quiet time.
19	  For the *waiting* sessions only, it also reads `last-response` and
20	  shows its first non-empty line, at most ten at a time, held in memory
21	  by (session, `last_stop_at_ms`). No new field on `SessionView`. This
22	  rests on For the owner "the card's excerpt"; if the owner wants the
23	  line on every card, the implementer builds the other branch: an
24	  additive, masked `excerpt: Option<String>` on `SessionView` (serde
25	  default, so older clients decode), computed on the frame from the same
26	  cache the card reads, which moves the fingerprints and needs the
27	  Swift fixtures rewritten (`SWITCHBOARD_WRITE_FIXTURES=1`).
28	- **"The device's scope in the header" has no endpoint.** Only the
29	  `/pair` reply carries `scope` (`src/app.rs:3660`–`3665`; Facts,
30	  Settled). A returning browser, and a browser whose scope the owner
31	  raised in the dialog, cannot learn it. Plan: one additive
32	  authenticated route, `GET /api/v1/me`.
33	- **"Revoked" and "never paired" are the same 401** (`authenticate`,
34	  `src/app.rs:3127`–`3156`). The plan adds no distinct code. The page
35	  keeps a non-secret marker `{server_id, spki_sha256, name}` after a
36	  pairing; a 401 with a marker whose key still equals `/info`'s is
37	  "revoked", a differing key or id is "identity changed, pair again"
38	  (a missing key remakes the identity and clears `devices.json`, so the
39	  key moves; `tests/remote.rs:1422`), and a 401 with no marker is "not
40	  paired".
41	- **"Compares the key in the URL with the one `/info` presents"** is a
42	  comparison against the host's own claim (`remote_info`,
43	  `src/app.rs:3568`); no browser API reads the peer certificate
44	  (Facts, Settled). It catches a wrong or stale host at the address; it
45	  does not stop an active relay that terminates TLS and forwards both
46	  `/info` and `/pair`. The dialog says so (UI, below).
47	- **"Keeps the token"**: with a cookie the page never holds it. The
48	  `/pair` reply to a browser omits `token` (below).
49	- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused"** stops being true for
50	  three exact paths. `docs/remote-client.md:306` ("Require pairing
51	  before anything but `/info` and `/pair`") and the checkbox hover text
52	  (`src/ui/remote.rs:113`) gain "and the page".
53	- **"The native text path takes the URL too, or the JSON as before"**:
54	  the plan keeps the JSON (the issue allows it). The Swift side is not
55	  touched; see decision 3.
56	- **"Revoke the phone and the page says so on its next request"** is
57	  met by the page's `/me` on load and by a socket close followed by a
58	  `/me`. A revoked page's open WebSocket is closed by the host
59	  (`RevokeDevice` drops the device's subscribers); the close carries no
60	  reason, so the page asks.
61	
62	## The decisions the issue asks for
63	
64	**1. Trust in the certificate: the click-through is the trust step.**
65	Why not the download: Apple's evaluation refuses today's certificate
66	even as the only trusted anchor, "certificate name does not match
67	input", because it has no subjectAltName (Facts, Settled, spike 23
68	`README.md:46`; `make_identity` builds `CertificateParams::new(vec![])`,
69	`src/adapters/remote.rs:102`). A trusted install therefore needs a
70	reissue with an IP SAN, bound to one address, so every DHCP change
71	means a new certificate and a new trust step on every phone (Settled,
72	`README.md:47`, `:50`). That is a larger feature than this page, and
73	the click-through needs none of it. What the click buys: the browser
74	accepts this certificate for this address. What it does not: it proves
75	nothing about who answered; on a hostile LAN an impostor can serve a
76	genuine-looking page and ask for the code. The code is single-use, the
77	window five minutes and three tries, and the owner compares the Key
78	line the page shows with the dialog's. The dialog says that in one
79	sentence. §5 is kept: before pairing the port serves `/info`, `/pair`
80	and the three page paths, nothing else.
81	Rests on two Unresolved lines: whether Safari offers a click-through for
82	a CN-only certificate on an IP, and whether the `wss://` socket then
83	connects (WebKit 41419 suggests it may not). The page is built for the
84	second regardless (polling fallback, UI). **Fallback if the owner's
85	device says there is no click-through:** `make_identity` takes the
86	advertised addresses and writes an IP SAN for each, the serverAuth EKU,
87	`not_before` kept at 1975 (the 825-day rule binds certificates issued
88	after 2019-07-01, Settled), the same key so the SPKI pin holds;
89	`identity.json` keeps the certificate, reissued when
90	`remote::local_address()` changes; a fourth page path `/switchboard.cer`
91	serves it; the dialog tells the owner to trust it under Certificate
92	Trust Settings (Settled, support.apple.com/en-us/102390).
93	
94	**2. The credential is a cookie.** `/pair`, when the body carries
95	`"credential": "cookie"`, sets
96	`__Host-sb-<server_id>=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`
97	(400 days, the cap, Settled) and leaves `token` out of the JSON.
98	Native clients do not send the field and get the token as before. The
99	name carries the server id because cookies are not isolated by port and
100	`__Host-` does not change that (Settled, RFC 6265 §8.5), so two hosts on
101	one IP do not overwrite each other. `SameSite=Strict` does not stop a
102	request from another port on the same IP (Settled, "site" ignores the
103	port), so the host checks `Origin` itself: a cookie-authenticated
104	request is refused 403 `origin` unless `Origin` equals
105	`https://<Host header>`, and a cookie-authenticated non-GET request or
106	upgrade without an `Origin` is refused too (a browser always sends one
107	for those; a plain GET may omit it and is side-effect free). A request
108	carrying a bearer header skips the check. The WebSocket handshake
109	carries the cookie and an `Origin` (Settled, WHATWG §2.2; RFC 6455
110	§10.2) and needs no subprotocol, so `respond_upgrade` is unchanged.
111	Rests on the Unresolved line "whether a `Secure` cookie on a
112	click-through origin is stored and sent". **Fallback if the owner's
113	device shows it is not:** the `/pair` reply keeps `token` for the page,
114	the page sends `Authorization: Bearer` on `fetch` and offers
115	`["sb1", <token>]` to `new WebSocket`; `read_request` keeps
116	`sec-websocket-protocol`, and `respond_upgrade` echoes `sb1` (a base64url
117	token fits RFC 6455's token rule, Settled); the token lives in
118	`localStorage`, which Safari deletes after seven days without use
119	(Settled), so the marker then reads "not paired" and the owner pairs
120	again.
121	
122	**3. One QR, two texts.** The QR becomes the URL
123	`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (a
124	smaller QR than the JSON: version 8 against 9, Settled, `README.md:61`).
125	"Copy invite" stays the JSON, so `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`,
126	the headset's paste field and the per-line scan
127	(`client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:111`,
128	`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`) and the
129	assertion at `tests/ui.rs:7474`–`7492` keep working, and the Swift tests
130	(not in CI) are not touched. A "Copy link" button copies the URL. This
131	is the "Keep JSON" branch of For the owner; if the owner wants URL only,
132	the implementer teaches `PairingInvite.parse`
133	(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`, `parse`) the URL with
134	`URLComponents` (an IPv6 literal arrives in brackets and is an
135	Unresolved parsing question), changes the assertion at
136	`tests/ui.rs:7486`, and adds a Swift fixture test.
137	
138	**4. The static paths.** Exactly `GET /` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
139	`GET /app.css` (`text/css; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js`
140	(`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`); the query is ignored, so
141	`/?code=…` is `/`. Any other method or path falls through to the frame
142	and is refused 404 as today (`/favicon.ico`, `/index.html`, `HEAD /`).
143	The page's icon is `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no browser asks
144	for `/favicon.ico` unprompted. Headers on the three:
145	`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`
146	(`'self'` covers `wss://` on the same host and port, Settled; the policy
147	is a header because `frame-ancestors` is ignored in a `<meta>`, Settled),
148	`Cache-Control: no-store` (the files change with the binary and are
149	small), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
150	`Connection: close`. These are answered **on the connection thread**,
151	before `RemoteIncoming` is built, so a page load costs no frame pass, no
152	inbox slot (`FRAMES`/64) and none of the eight drains per pass
153	(`DRAIN_PER_PASS`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:580`), and it works with the
154	app hidden. `Connection: close` ends the thread and so frees the
155	connection's slot in the four-connection unauthenticated pool at once.
156	Their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120`, beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE`
157	and `INFO_PER_MINUTE` (`:583`–`:584`), through `Limits::limited`
158	(`:631`), 429 as the others. A page opened with no code and no cookie
159	shows "This browser is not paired" and how to pair (Remote devices…,
160	Allow pairing, scan the QR); a code whose window has closed shows the
161	host's `pairing_closed` text.
162	Rests on the Unresolved line about Safari's parallel connections against
163	`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`. The page loads its two files after the HTML
164	and calls `/info` and then `/pair` one at a time, so at most three
165	connections are open at once, and it retries a network error three times
166	300 ms apart. **Fallback if the owner's device still sees a refused
167	connection:** raise `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` to 6 and amend §4.1's first
168	bound; the pools stay separate.
169	
170	**5. Where the page lives and how it is tested.** `web/index.html`,
171	`web/app.css`, `web/app.js` at the repo root, embedded by
172	`src/adapters/web.rs` with `include_str!`. No build step, no
173	dependency, no `build.rs`. `Cargo.toml` excludes only
174	`vendor/egui_term` (`:91`), so `web/` ships in the crate. Tests below.
175	
176	**6. The device record.** No change (Record, below).
177	
178	## The record
179	
180	Nothing changes on disk. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`)
181	like any other: `name` is the `device_name` `/pair` already takes
182	(`src/app.rs:3650`, cut to 64 characters by `new_device`), `scope` comes
183	from the pairing window, it is listed and revoked in the dialog as today.
184	The page offers a name field defaulted from the user agent ("Safari on
185	iPhone", "Chrome on Android"; an iPad reads as "Safari on Mac", Settled),
186	which the owner can edit before pairing, so the host parses no user
187	agent. Nothing marks a device as a browser. Rehydration is today's: the
188	hash of the cookie's token goes through `device_by_token`, so a browser
189	paired yesterday is authenticated today.
190	Schema versions today: `SCHEMA_VERSION` 16 (`src/core/model.rs:12`),
191	`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION` 7 (`:612`), `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1
192	(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). No serialized type changes, so none bumps;
193	if a ticket landing in parallel changes one, that ticket's bump is its
194	own (from the value at implementation time, plus one).
195	
196	## The signals
197	
198	- `RemoteRequest` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:360`) gains `cookie`,
199	  `origin` and `host`, taken in `read_request` (`:444`) beside
200	  `authorization`, which today is the only credential kept. Like the
201	  bearer they are never logged; `refuse` (`src/app.rs:3754`) logs method
202	  and path only and no log line prints a query or token (Facts, Settled).
203	  `RemoteRequest::cookie_origin_ok()` is the Origin rule of decision 2.
204	- `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains `set_cookie: Option<String>`; every
205	  literal in `src/app.rs` (about fourteen, e.g. `:1664`, `:1679`,
206	  `:2365`, `:2754`, `:3570`, `:3723`, `:3736`, `:3767`) and
207	  `adapters/remote.rs:829` gets `set_cookie: None`.
208	- `respond` (`:530`), which hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json`,
209	  becomes a wrapper over `respond_with(w, status, content_type, extra
210	  headers, body)`; the page and the `Set-Cookie` use the second.
211	- `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`): bearer first; else the cookie
212	  named for this host's server id, then the Origin rule. A refusal is
213	  403 `origin` ("this request did not come from the page the host
214	  served") or the same 401s as today.
215	- The events socket: nothing new. `changed` with `session`, `sessions`,
216	  `projects`, `waiting`, `conversation` and `screen` kinds (the
217	  spec's §4.4) is all the page reads; it sends
218	  `{"type":"watch","resource":{"kind":"screen"|"conversation","id":…}}`
219	  for the open session (`src/app.rs:1720`).
220	
221	## The actions and effects
222	
223	None. No `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no port method: everything is
224	adapter, `serve_remote` and the page. In `serve_remote` (`:3017`) `/pair`
225	reads the `credential` field and builds the `Set-Cookie`; a new
226	authenticated arm `("GET", ["me"])` answers `{device_id, name, scope}`
227	in the usual envelope. `core/remote.rs` gains one pure function,
228	`pairing_url(addr: SocketAddr, server_id, spki_sha256, code) -> String`
229	(`SocketAddr`'s display brackets an IPv6 literal; the code's alphabet
230	and hex need no percent-encoding).
231	
232	## The page
233	
234	`app.js`, plain ES2020, no `eval`, `innerHTML` or `document.write`
235	(text through `textContent`, which is the whole XSS argument for a page
236	that can type into an agent). In order:
237	
238	1. First statement: read `location.search`, then
239	   `history.replaceState(null, "", location.pathname)`; the code lives
240	   in a variable only, never in storage. (Whether the browser's global
241	   history or iCloud tab sync kept the first URL is Unresolved; the
242	   dialog's text does not promise it did not.)
243	2. `GET /api/v1/info`. With an invite: if `spki_sha256` or `server_id`
244	   differs from `key`/`id`, say "this is not the host the code was made
245	   for" and send nothing. Else show the host name, the short key (four
246	   groups of four, as the dialog does), the name field and a Pair
247	   button; the tap posts `/pair {spki_sha256: key, code, device_name,
248	   credential: "cookie"}`. `wrong_code`, `wrong_key`, `pairing_closed`
249	   and `rate_limited` are worded plainly.
250	3. Without an invite: `GET /me`; 200 shows the list, 401 per the
251	   marker (departures, above).
252	4. The list follows §4.4: open the socket, wait for `hello`, fetch
253	   `projects`, `waiting` and each project's `sessions` (the listing
254	   has no global form), apply buffered events by revision (an event
255	   past a snapshot's revision refetches that resource). A "Waiting on
256	   you" band comes first, then projects, waiting sessions first in each
257	   and marked; each row shows kind (`claude`, `codex`, `shell`,
258	   `command`, `service`), the card word, `waiting_reason` and the
259	   excerpt of departure 1. The header shows the host name from `/info`,
260	   and this device's name and scope from `/me`.
261	5. A session view: `claude`/`codex` read `last-response`, falling back
262	   to `screen` when it is empty; the rest read `screen`; a session not
263	   running shows its liveness and exit code (run output is a later
264	   issue, per "Not in this cut"). It watches the key and refetches on
265	   `changed`, and on its own every thirty seconds (§4.4).
266	6. The reply box exists only when `/me` says `control`. A send posts
267	   `{op: <uuid>, text}` to `/sessions/{id}/send`; the op is kept in
268	   `sessionStorage` until the reply is read, a timeout is followed by
269	   `GET /ops/{op}`, never a resend (§4.5), and a reload with a pending
270	   op asks `/ops/{op}` first. A 403 `scope` hides the box again. The
271	   op id is `crypto.randomUUID()` where present, else 16 bytes from
272	   `crypto.getRandomValues` (the Unresolved line on certificate-error
273	   pages).
274	7. Live updates: if `hello` does not arrive within five seconds, or the
275	   socket closes before `hello` twice running, the page says "live
276	   updates unavailable, refreshing every 5 s" and polls `waiting` and the
277	   open session every five seconds, projects and sessions every
278	   fifteen. This is the answer to the `wss://` Unresolved line and
279	   stays in whichever way the owner's run goes.
280	
281	## The UI
282	
283	`src/ui/remote.rs`: the QR (`qr_texture`, `:280`) encodes
284	`pairing_url(...)`; `payload` stays the JSON for "Copy invite"; a "Copy
285	link" button beside it. Address, port and the cache key (`draft.qr`
286	keyed by code, `:168`–`:172`) as today. The scan line becomes: "Scan with a
287	phone camera to open the page, or paste the invite into a client.
288	The browser will warn about the certificate; accepting it is the trust
289	step, so check that the page shows this Key. Grants {scope} scope. Open
290	for five minutes or three wrong codes." The checkbox hover (`:113`)
291	ends "only paired devices get past /info and the page". With the port on
292	loopback the address in the URL is still the LAN address (existing
293	behaviour, now inherited); listed as a known gap, not fixed here.
294	
295	## The tests
296	
297	- `src/core/tests.rs`: `pairing_url` for an IPv4 and an IPv6 address,
298	  parameter order, no encoding needed.
299	- `src/adapters/remote.rs` unit: `read_request` keeps `cookie`,
300	  `origin` and `host`; `respond_with` writes the headers and
301	  `Content-Length`; `cookie_origin_ok` over GET/POST/upgrade with
302	  and without `Origin`.
303	- `tests/remote.rs`, with a new `http_full` beside `http`
304	  (`:245`, which keeps only status and body and matches
305	  `Content-Length:` by exact case) returning headers, a `Cookie` and
306	  `Origin` option:
307	  1. The three paths answer unpaired, **with the test never driving
308	     `serve_pending`** (proving the connection thread served them), with
309	     the exact headers above; `HEAD /`, `POST /`, `/index.html`,
310	     `/favicon.ico` stay 404 JSON. Amend
311	     `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired`
312	     (`:426`) and `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect`
313	     (`:682`) for `GET /`.
314	  2. The embedded page references only paths the host serves: every
315	     `src`/`href` in `index.html` is one of the three paths or `data:`;
316	     every `/api/v1/…` literal in `app.js`, with ids filled in from the
317	     seeded records, answers something other than `not available on this
318	     port` for a paired device. `index.html` has no inline `<script>`,
319	     `<style>` or `style=`; no file contains `eval(`, `innerHTML` or
320	     `document.write`; `history.replaceState` precedes the first
321	     `fetch(` in `app.js`.
322	  3. Pairing end to end as the CLI does, with the host's own client:
323	     `/pair` with `credential: "cookie"` returns no `token`, and
324	     `Set-Cookie` equals the exact string of decision 2; `GET /me` with
325	     only that cookie answers the name and scope; a raised scope shows
326	     on the next `/me`; a wrong cookie 401; a bearer-only pair is
327	     unchanged (the existing pairing tests stay as they are).
328	  4. The Origin rule: cookie plus a foreign `Origin` 403 `origin`; a
329	     cookie `POST …/send` with no `Origin` 403, with the right one runs
330	     once per op and a repeat is answered from the log; a cookie `GET`
331	     with no `Origin` 200; a bearer request ignores `Origin`.
332	  5. The socket: `subscribe_at` gains a cookie-and-origin variant;
333	     `hello` arrives with the right `Origin`, the handshake is refused
334	     without one or with another port's; a revoke closes it and the
335	     next `/me` is 401 (`RevokeDevice`).
336	  6. `PAGE_PER_MINUTE`: the 121st page request in a minute is 429,
337	     while `/info` still answers. Three page loads in sequence leave
338	     the unauthenticated pool empty, and
339	     `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients`
340	     (`:3226`) passes unchanged.
341	- `tests/ui.rs:7424`: "Copy link" puts an `https://` URL with `code`,
342	  `key` and `id` on the clipboard (the code equal to the window's, the
343	  key to the identity's); "Copy invite" still copies the JSON
344	  (`:7474`–`7492` unchanged).
345	- No Swift test or fixture changes: no native client reads `/me` or
346	  the page, and `/info` and the views are untouched, so the fixture set
347	  (`write_fixtures`, `tests/remote.rs:1587`) does not move.
348	- No browser is driven (nothing in the tree, no keystroke injection).
349	  What needs a device is listed in the status section as not yet run:
350	  the acceptance sequence (scan with a phone camera, accept the
351	  warning, see the sessions, a session that starts waiting moves to the
352	  top, a reply arrives, revoke and the next request says so) on the
353	  devices the owner names, plus the Unresolved lines: click-through for
354	  the CN-only certificate, the `wss://` socket, the cookie's storage, the
355	  connection fan-out, the camera banner. No new spike directory:
356	  nothing here is runnable without a device, and the certificate
357	  question has spike 23; the owner's results go into spike 23's
358	  `README.md`.
359	
360	## Documents
361	
362	- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 (page paths answered on the connection
363	  thread, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE`), §4.3 (rows for `/`, `/app.css`, `/app.js`
364	  and `/me`), §5 (the pre-pairing bullet at `:306`, the token bullet "sent
365	  only as a bearer header" to say a browser's is a cookie, the pairing
366	  bullet to say the QR is a URL, the Origin rule, what the key
367	  comparison does and does not prove).
368	- `docs/design.md`: the "Remote client" status section (ends before
369	  `:3585`): what is built, and the not-yet-run list above, and the
370	  known gap about the loopback address.
371	- `README.md`: Layout rows for `web/` and `src/adapters/web.rs`, the
372	  edited `adapters/remote.rs` row (page paths, the page rate window),
373	  and a Development line: with `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` set and
374	  `pairing <code>` / `remote-listen` script lines, the page is at
375	  `https://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. No new `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line: the
376	  state is reachable with the existing ones.
377	- `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased: a browser page on the remote port,
378	  paired by scanning the dialog's QR.
379	
380	## Commit message
381	
382	Serve a browser page on the remote port, paired from a URL that carries the code
383	
384	## Contract additions
385	
386	- Routes: `GET /` (`text/html`), `GET /app.css`, `GET /app.js`, answered
387	  on the connection thread before pairing; `GET /api/v1/me`
388	  (`{device_id, name, scope}`, any paired device).
389	- `/pair` request field `credential: "cookie"`; with it the reply
390	  carries `Set-Cookie: __Host-sb-<server_id>=…` and no `token`. The
391	  host accepts that cookie as a credential, with the Origin rule,
392	  beside the bearer header.
